newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan official won't comment on land tax report.
newsitem.headline: Japan official won't comment on land tax report.

text.p: An official of Japan's National Land Agency said on Friday he would not comment on a newspaper report that an advisory panel to the prime minister had urged reform of land taxes to help boost liquidity in the real estate market.
The official said the advisory council on land policies had been discussing land policy reform since April and was likely to unveil its proposal in late November or early December.
He said the proposal had yet to be finalised and would not comment on the report in the mass circulation Yomiuri Shimbun.

Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto asked the advisory body in April to review the nation's basic land policy to cope with structural changes such as falling land prices and a rapid rise in the proportion of old people.
Another National Land Agency official said recently it was the first time in five years that the government had reviewed its basic land policy.

The advisory body is now discussing policies to promote the effective use of land from a long-term standpoint. Since 1991, Japan has adopted a land policy aimed at curbing soaring land prices, he said.
